While working on our Schreier graph formalization, we noticed that Combinatorics.SimpleGraph has solid infrastructure for adjacency matrices (AdjMatrix, walk counting via adjMatrix_pow_apply_eq_card_walk) and Laplacians (LapMatrix), but there doesn't seem to be any bridge to the eigenvalue/eigenvector API in LinearAlgebra.Eigenspace.

Concretely, things like the graph spectrum, spectral gap, Cheeger inequality, or expander mixing lemma don't appear to be formalized anywhere. Is anyone aware of ongoing work in this direction, or is it genuinely untouched?

We've been building application-specific spectral lemmas for our project (block diagonalization of covering graphs, Rayleigh quotient bounds, Perron-Frobenius consequences for symmetric adjacency matrices) and some of the intermediate results feel general enough to upstream — but we'd want to coordinate rather than duplicate if someone else is working on this.
I'm sorta working on this, #39627 is my 3rd PR on the subject, but everything is pretty early days

Snir Broshi said:

I'm sorta working on this, #39627 is my 3rd PR on the subject, but everything is pretty early days

That's incredible timing! I'm looking at #39627 now (0 is always an eigenvalue for the Laplacian).

We are actually sitting on a stack of 0-sorry proofs for the next logical steps for that API. Specifically, we've formalized walk-propagation for powers of symmetric matrices (matrix_pow_pos_of_walk) and proved that for connected support graphs, the top eigenspace is 1-dimensional (connected_eigenvector_unique), along with constant-sign theorems for the eigenvector.

We're currently extracting these out of our application-specific code into a clean Mathlib-compliant module. Since you're actively laying the groundwork for Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Spectral, would you want us to open these as a companion PR that builds directly on top of your #39627, or should we collaborate on a mega-PR?

Snir Broshi said:

I'm sorta working on this, #39627 is my 3rd PR on the subject, but everything is pretty early days

Update: extraction is done. Here's the full file: https://github.com/sneed-and-feed/adelic-spectral-zeta/blob/main/formalization/Formalization/MathlibSpectral.lean

447 lines, 0 sorry, compiles against current Mathlib. The full lemma list:

  • matrix_pow_nonneg — powers of nonneg matrices stay nonneg
  • matrix_pow_pos_of_walk — A^k i j > 0 whenever a length-k walk exists in the support graph
  • eigenvector_zero_of_walk — nonneg eigenvector zero propagates along walks
  • connected_eigenvector_unique — connected support graph ⟹ top eigenspace is 1-dimensional
  • eigenvector_constant_sign_matrix — PF eigenvector has constant sign
  • abs_eigenvector_of_symmetric — |w| is also an eigenvector for the same eigenvalue
  • pf_eigenvalue_is_max — PF eigenvalue dominates all others
  • mu_B_le_max_eig' — eigenvalue bound via Hermitian spectral decomposition

These pick up right where your #39627 leaves off. Let me know how you'd like to coordinate.

Since you appear to be a heavy LLM user I am not interested in collaborating, but you're welcome to PR your results whether they depend on my PRs or not!
I think it's worth reiterating that the Mathlib community is aware that LLMs can formalize such results, and 0-sorry is a very low-bar when it comes to Mathlib standards.
Since you haven't opened any PRs before I have no idea what the quality of your code is, but if it's great or you're willing to put in the work then it would be amazing if you could build up spectral graph theory!

Totally fair on all counts. I appreciate the directness.

You're right that the code as-is is almost certainly not Mathlib-style — I haven't gone through the linting, naming conventions, docstrings, or the kind of proof refactoring that a real review would demand. "It compiles with 0 sorry" is the starting line, not the finish line, and I understand that.

I'll work on getting a proper PR together that meets the actual standards. If it's not up to par, the reviewers will tell me and I'll learn. Thanks for the pointer — I'll build on your foundation rather than duplicate it.

And now I feel like I'm also conversing with an LLM.
I'll just note that you should read the AI guidelines, and I look forward to seeing good quality PRs from you!

The module is now refactored to comply with Mathlib standards. Any early review for anti-patterns would be appreciated before I actually investigate the full formal PR.

It's not close to complying with Mathlib standards (btw we don't require a docstring on every lemma), but that's okay! The review process is what helps contributors learn and adjust to the standards (assuming there's a human on the other side).
